path: Groups isomorphic to their normal subgroups

results.title: Hall's question on groups isomorphic to their nontrivial normal subgroups (Kourovka 12.45)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that every nontrivial group that is isomorphic to each of its nontrivial normal subgroups is free of infinite rank (isomorphic to the free group on an infinite set), simple, or infinite cyclic.

results.title: A group isomorphic to its nontrivial normal subgroups need not be free of infinite rank, simple or infinite cyclic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A group isomorphic to its nontrivial normal subgroups need not be free of infinite rank, simple or infinite cyclic. There is a nontrivial group $G$ that is isomorphic to each of its nontrivial normal subgroups and is neither free of infinite rank (isomorphic to the free group on an infinite set), nor simple, nor infinite cyclic. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 12.45 is negative (V. N. Obraztsov, 1997).

results.title: Locally finite groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is finite.

results.title: Locally soluble subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is locally soluble if every finitely generated subgroup of $H$ is soluble.

results.title: Centralizer dimension at most $k$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ has $c$-dimension at most $k$ if every strictly decreasing chain $C_G(X_0) > C_G(X_1) > \cdots > C_G(X_m)$ of centralizers of subsets $X_0, \dots, X_m$ of $G$ has length $m \le k$.

results.title: Minimal normal subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $M$ of a group $Q$ is a minimal normal subgroup if $M$ is normal in $Q$, $M \ne \{1\}$, and every normal subgroup $N$ of $Q$ with $N \le M$ is either $\{1\}$ or $M$.

results.title: Socle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The socle of a group $Q$ is the subgroup of $Q$ generated by all minimal normal subgroups of $Q$; it is the trivial subgroup when $Q$ has no minimal normal subgroup.

results.title: Preimage of the socle of a quotient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a normal subgroup $R$ of a group $G$, the preimage in $G$ of the socle of $G/R$ under the quotient map $G \to G/R$.

results.title: The (2, 4, 8) triangle group
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The $(2, 4, 8)$ triangle group is the group with presentation $\langle x, y \mid x^2 = y^4 = (xy)^8 = 1 \rangle$.

results.title: Wiegold's question on 2-group quotients of the (2, 4, 8) triangle group (Kourovka 16.101)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there are an uncountable index set $I$ and normal subgroups $N_i$ of $\Gamma = \langle x, y \mid x^2 = y^4 = (xy)^8 = 1 \rangle$, for $i \in I$, such that every quotient $\Gamma / N_i$ is an infinite $2$-group (a group in which every element has order a power of $2$), and $\Gamma / N_i \cong \Gamma / N_j$ only when $i = j$.

results.title: Uncountably many infinite 2-group quotients of the (2, 4, 8) triangle group (Kourovka 16.101)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma = \langle x, y \mid x^2 = y^4 = (xy)^8 = 1 \rangle$. There are an uncountable index set $I$ and normal subgroups $N_i$ of $\Gamma$, for $i \in I$, such that every quotient $\Gamma / N_i$ is an infinite $2$-group (a group in which every element has order a power of $2$), and $\Gamma / N_i \cong \Gamma / N_j$ only when $i = j$. So Wiegold's question has a positive answer.

results.title: Additive Hilbert 90 for cyclic extensions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L/K$ be a finite-dimensional Galois extension and let $\sigma$ be a $K$-algebra automorphism of $L$ that generates its Galois group, that is, every $K$-algebra automorphism of $L$ is an integer power of $\sigma$. Then the kernel of the trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K} \colon L \to K$ equals the image of the $K$-linear map $\sigma - 1 \colon L \to L$, $y \mapsto \sigma(y) - y$.

results.title: Additive Hilbert 90, pointwise form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L/K$ be a finite-dimensional Galois extension and let $\sigma$ be a $K$-algebra automorphism of $L$ that generates its Galois group, that is, every $K$-algebra automorphism of $L$ is an integer power of $\sigma$. If $x \in L$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(x) = 0$, then there is $y \in L$ with $\sigma(y) - y = x$.

results.title: Sum-product sets cover the integers modulo a prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $A_1, A_2, A_3, D$ be subsets of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $|A_1| |A_2| |A_3| |D| > p^3$. Then every residue class modulo $p$ can be written as $a_1 d + a_2 + a_3$ with $a_1 \in A_1$, $d \in D$, $a_2 \in A_2$ and $a_3 \in A_3$; that is, $A_1 D + A_2 + A_3 = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Diagonal congruences in $k$ variables are solvable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $k \ge 1$. For all integers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ not divisible by $p$ and every integer $c$, there are integers $x_1, \dots, x_k$ with $a_1 x_1^k + \dots + a_k x_k^k \equiv c \pmod p$.

results.title: Rademacher measure on the integer units
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Rademacher measure is the uniform probability measure on the two integer units $\{-1, 1\}$.

results.title: Each Rademacher sign has probability one half
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For each integer unit $x \in \{-1, 1\}$, the Rademacher measure of the singleton $\{x\}$ is $1/2$.

results.title: Rademacher family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\Omega$. A family $(X_p)$, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$ into the units of $\mathbb{Z}$ is a Rademacher family for $\mu$ when every $X_p$ is measurable, every $X_p$ has law the Rademacher measure (the uniform measure on $\{-1, 1\}$) under $\mu$, and the family is mutually independent under $\mu$.

results.title: Existence of a Rademacher family
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a measurable space $\Omega$, a probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ and a family $(X_p)$, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$ into the units of $\mathbb{Z}$ that is a Rademacher family for $\mu$.

results.title: Prime sign of a natural number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X = (X_p)$ be a family, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$ into the units of $\mathbb{Z}$. For a natural number $n$ and $\omega \in \Omega$, the prime sign of $n$ at $\omega$ is the integer $X_n(\omega)$ if $n$ is prime and $1$ otherwise.

results.title: Measurability of the prime signs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(X_p)$ be a Rademacher family for a measure $\mu$ on a measurable space $\Omega$. For every natural number $n$, the map $\omega \mapsto \varepsilon_n(\omega)$ from $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{Z}$ is measurable, where the prime sign $\varepsilon_n(\omega)$ is $X_n(\omega)$ if $n$ is prime and $1$ otherwise.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(X_p)_p$ be a family of maps $X_p : \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$ indexed by the primes, and let $\omega \in \Omega$. The Rademacher random multiplicative function at $\omega$ is the arithmetic function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ with $f(0) = 0$ and

results.title: Formula for the Rademacher random multiplicative function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X = (X_p)$ be a family, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$, let $\omega \in \Omega$, and let $f$ be the Rademacher random multiplicative function of $X$ at $\omega$. For every natural number $n \neq 0$, $f(n) = \mu(n)^2 \prod_{p \mid n} \varepsilon_p(\omega)$, where $\mu$ is the Möbius function, the product runs over the distinct primes $p$ dividing $n$, and…

results.title: The Rademacher random multiplicative function on squarefree numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X = (X_p)$ be a family, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$, let $\omega \in \Omega$, and let $f$ be the Rademacher random multiplicative function of $X$ at $\omega$. For every squarefree natural number $n$, $f(n) = \prod_{p \mid n} \varepsilon_p(\omega)$, the product of the prime signs $\varepsilon_p(\omega)$ at $\omega$ over the distinct primes $p$ dividing $n$.

results.title: The Rademacher random multiplicative function vanishes off squarefree numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X = (X_p)$ be a family, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$, let $\omega \in \Omega$, and let $f$ be the Rademacher random multiplicative function of $X$ at $\omega$. Then $f(n) = 0$ for every natural number $n$ that is not squarefree, including $n = 0$.

results.title: The Rademacher random multiplicative function is multiplicative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X = (X_p)$ be a family, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$, and let $\omega \in \Omega$. The Rademacher random multiplicative function $f$ of $X$ at $\omega$ satisfies $f(1) = 1$ and $f(mn) = f(m) f(n)$ for all coprime natural numbers $m$ and $n$.

results.title: Value of the Rademacher function at a prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(X_p)_p$ be a family of maps $X_p : \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$ indexed by the primes, let $\omega \in \Omega$, and let $f$ be the associated Rademacher random multiplicative function at $\omega$. For every prime $p$, the value $f(p)$ is the sign assigned to $p$, that is, $f(p) = X_p(\omega)$.

results.title: The Rademacher random multiplicative function vanishes at prime squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X = (X_p)$ be a family, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$, let $\omega \in \Omega$, and let $f$ be the Rademacher random multiplicative function of $X$ at $\omega$. Then $f(p^2) = 0$ for every prime $p$.

results.title: Measurability of the Rademacher random multiplicative function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(X_p)$ be a Rademacher family for a measure $\mu$ on a measurable space $\Omega$, and for $\omega \in \Omega$ let $f_\omega$ be the Rademacher random multiplicative function of $(X_p)$ at $\omega$. For every natural number $n$, the map $\omega \mapsto f_\omega(n)$ from $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{Z}$ is measurable.

results.title: Partial sums of the Rademacher multiplicative function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given signs $X_p(\omega) \in \{-1, 1\}$ indexed by the primes $p$ and a sample point $\omega$, and given $N \in \mathbb{N}$, the partial sum $S_N(\omega)$ is the real number $\sum_{m=1}^{N} f_\omega(m)$, where $f_\omega$ is the Rademacher multiplicative function of the signs $X_p(\omega)$: $f_\omega(m) = \prod_{p \mid m} X_p(\omega)$ for squarefree $m$ and $f_\omega(m) = 0$ otherwise.

results.title: Signed power-of-two sums
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$, $s$ and $t$, an integer $n$ is a signed power-of-two sum with coefficients in $\{-1, m\}$ over the range $s \le j \le t$ if $n = \sum_{j=s}^{t} \lambda_j 2^j$ for some integers $\lambda_j$ with every $\lambda_j \in \{-1, m\}$.

results.title: Example of a signed power-of-two sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The integer $1$ can be written as $\sum_{j=0}^{1} \lambda_j 2^j$ with every $\lambda_j \in \{-1, 3\}$, namely $1 = 3 \cdot 2^0 + (-1) \cdot 2^1$.

results.title: Interval and congruence characterization of signed power-of-two sums
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $s \le t$ be natural numbers and put $L = t - s + 1$. An integer $n$ can be written as $\sum_{j=s}^{t} \lambda_j 2^j$ with every $\lambda_j \in \{-1, m\}$ if and only if $-2^s (2^L - 1) \le n \le 2^s m (2^L - 1)$ and $n \equiv -2^s (2^L - 1) \pmod{2^s (m + 1)}$.

results.title: Extending a signed power-of-two sum to a longer range
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 1$, $s$, $t$ and $\alpha$ be natural numbers, let $\beta = \nu_2(m + 1)$ be the exponent of $2$ in $m + 1$, and suppose that $s + \beta \le t + 1$ and $2^\alpha \equiv 1 \pmod{(m + 1)/2^\beta}$. If an integer $n$ can be written as $\sum_{j=s}^{t} \lambda_j 2^j$ with every $\lambda_j \in \{-1, m\}$, then $n$ can also be written as $\sum_{j=s}^{t+\alpha} \mu_j 2^j$ with every $\mu_j \in \{-1, m\}$.

results.title: Integers that are one plus a signed sum of powers of two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An integer $n$ can be written as $n = 1 + \sum_{j=1}^{k} \lambda_j 2^j$ for some $k \ge 1$ and some $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_k \in \{-1, 1\}$ if and only if $n \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.

results.title: Model space $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ for Darboux's theorem
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the model space is $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, the Euclidean space of dimension $2n$ with coordinates indexed by $0, 1, \dots, 2n - 1$ and the standard inner product.

results.title: Index of the $i$-th $p$-coordinate in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $i \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, the index of the $i$-th $p$-coordinate among the coordinates $0, \dots, 2n - 1$ of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ is $i$ itself.

results.title: Index of the $i$-th $q$-coordinate in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $i \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, the index of the $i$-th $q$-coordinate among the coordinates $0, \dots, 2n - 1$ of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ is $i + n$.

results.title: Darboux normal form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $e_0, \dots, e_{2n-1}$ be the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. A continuous alternating 2-form $\omega$ on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ is in Darboux normal form if for all $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ we have $\omega(e_i, e_{n+j}) = 1$ when $i = j$ and $0$ otherwise, $\omega(e_i, e_j) = 0$, and $\omega(e_{n+i}, e_{n+j}) = 0$.

results.title: Müntz–Szász theorem for integer exponents
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Lambda : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be strictly increasing with $\Lambda(0) = 0$. The real linear span of the monomials $x \mapsto x^{\Lambda(n)}$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, restricted to $[0, 1]$, is dense in $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ with the uniform norm if and only if the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} 1/\Lambda(n+1)$ diverges, that is, the sequence $(1/\Lambda(n+1))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is not summable.

results.title: Runge's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be compact, let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be open with $K \subseteq U$, and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be analytic at every point of $U$. Then for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there are complex polynomials $p$ and $q$ such that $q(z) \ne 0$ for every $z \in K$ and $|f(z) - p(z)/q(z)| < \varepsilon$ for every $z \in K$.

results.title: The conditional distribution kernel is a regular conditional distribution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty standard Borel space, $\mu$ a finite measure on $\alpha$, and $X : \alpha \to \beta$, $Y : \alpha \to \Omega$ measurable maps. Then the conditional distribution of $Y$ given $X$ under $\mu$, the kernel from $\beta$ to $\Omega$ obtained by disintegrating the joint law of $(X, Y)$ under $\mu$, is a regular conditional distribution of $Y$ given $X$ under $\mu$.

results.title: Existence of regular conditional distributions (kernel form)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty standard Borel space, $\mu$ a finite measure on $\alpha$, and $X : \alpha \to \beta$, $Y : \alpha \to \Omega$ measurable maps. Then there exists a kernel $\kappa$ from $\beta$ to $\Omega$ that is a regular conditional distribution of $Y$ given $X$ under $\mu$; in particular $\kappa$ is a Markov kernel.

results.title: Existence of measure-valued regular conditional distributions given a sub-σ-algebra

Then some family of measures on $\Omega$ indexed by $\alpha$ is a measure-valued regular conditional distribution of $Y$ given $\mathcal{G}$ under $\mu$.

results.title: Existence of measure-valued regular conditional distributions given a random variable

results.title: Sum-free sets modulo $m$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $l$, a set $A$ of integers is $l$-sum-free modulo $m$ if there are no $x_1, \dots, x_l, y \in A$ (repetitions allowed) with $x_1 + \dots + x_l \equiv y \pmod{m}$.

results.title: Sum-free partitions modulo $m$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$, $k$, $l$ and $n$, the range $\{1, \dots, n\}$ admits a partition into $k$ classes that are $l$-sum-free modulo $m$ if there is a coloring $c$ of the natural numbers with $k$ colors such that, for each color $j$, the set of integers $a$ with $1 \le a \le n$ and $c(a) = j$ is $l$-sum-free modulo $m$. Classes may be empty; for $k = 0$ there is no coloring, so the property fails for every $n$,…

results.title: Modular Schur number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$, $k$ and $l$, the generalized Schur number modulo $m$, written $S_m(k, l)$, is the largest natural number $n$ such that $\{1, \dots, n\}$ admits a partition into $k$ (possibly empty) classes that are each $l$-sum-free modulo $m$; it is $0$ when there is no largest such $n$.

results.title: The empty range has a sum-free partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $m$, $l$ and $k \ge 1$, the empty range $\{1, \dots, 0\}$ admits a partition into $k$ classes that are $l$-sum-free modulo $m$.

results.title: Sets containing a multiple of the modulus are not sum-free
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ and $l$ be natural numbers and let $A$ be a set of integers. If $A$ contains an integer $a$ divisible by $m$, then $A$ is not $l$-sum-free modulo $m$: the sum of $l$ copies of $a$ is congruent to $a$ modulo $m$.

results.title: $\{1\}$ is $2$-sum-free modulo $3$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The singleton $\{1\}$ is $2$-sum-free modulo $3$, since $1 + 1 \not\equiv 1 \pmod{3}$.

results.title: When the singleton $\{1\}$ is sum-free
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $l$ be natural numbers. The singleton $\{1\}$ is not $l$-sum-free modulo $m$ if and only if $l \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$.

results.title: Vanishing of modular Schur numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$, $k$ and $l$ be positive integers. The generalized Schur number $S_m(k, l)$, the largest $n$ such that $\{1, \dots, n\}$ admits a partition into $k$ classes that are $l$-sum-free modulo $m$, equals $0$ if and only if $l \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$.

results.title: Congruence upper bound for modular Schur numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$, $k$, $l$ and $a$ be natural numbers with $k \ge 1$, $l \ge 1$ and $1 \le a \le m - 1$, and let $d = \gcd(a, m)$. If $l \equiv 1 \pmod{m/d}$, then the generalized Schur number $S_m(k, l)$ modulo $m$ satisfies $S_m(k, l) < a$.

results.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo an even number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$, $l$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $k \ge 2$, $n \ge 2$, $l \ge 1$ and $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod{2n}$, and let $S_{2n}(k, l)$ be the generalized Schur number modulo $2n$. If $l \equiv n + 1 \pmod{2n}$, then $S_{2n}(k, l) = 1$; otherwise $S_{2n}(k, l) \ge 2$.

results.title: Modular Schur numbers attaining $m - 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $l \ge 2$ and $m \ge 2$ be natural numbers such that $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod{d}$ for every divisor $d \ne 1$ of $m$, and let $k \ge m - 1$. Then the generalized Schur number $S_m(k, l)$, the largest $n$ such that $\{1, \dots, n\}$ admits a partition into $k$ classes that are $l$-sum-free modulo $m$, equals $m - 1$.

results.title: Lower bound for modular Schur numbers modulo a prime power
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $i$ and $l$ be positive integers with $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod{p}$, and let $1 \le k \le p - 1$. Then the generalized Schur number $S_{p^i}(k, l)$, the largest $n$ such that $\{1, \dots, n\}$ admits a partition into $k$ classes that are $l$-sum-free modulo $p^i$, is at least $k$.

results.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo a prime power for many classes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $i$ and $l$ be positive integers with $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod p$, and let $k$ be a natural number with $k \ge p^i - 1$. Then the generalized Schur number modulo $p^i$ satisfies $S_{p^i}(k, l) = p^i - 1$.

results.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo a prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $l$ be a positive integer with $l \ge p - 1$ and $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod p$. Then the generalized Schur number modulo $p$ satisfies $S_p(k, l) = k$ for every natural number $k$ with $1 \le k \le p - 1$, and $S_p(k, l) = p - 1$ for every natural number $k \ge p - 1$.

results.title: Singletons are sum-free modulo a prime power
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $i$ and $l$ be positive integers with $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod{p}$, and let $a$ be a natural number not divisible by $p^i$. Then the singleton $\{a\}$ is $l$-sum-free modulo $p^i$.

results.title: Elements of a sum-free pair are congruent modulo $p$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $i$ be a positive integer, and let $l$ be a natural number with $l \ge p^i - 1$ and $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod{p}$. If $a$ and $b$ are natural numbers such that $\{a, b\}$ is $l$-sum-free modulo $p^i$, then $a \equiv b \pmod{p}$.

results.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo $2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all positive integers $k$ and $l$, the modular Schur number $S_2(k, l)$ equals $0$ when $l$ is odd and equals $1$ when $l$ is even.

results.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo 3
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers and let $S_3(k, l)$ be the generalized Schur number modulo $3$. If $l \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, then $S_3(k, l) = 0$. Otherwise $S_3(1, l) = 1$, and $S_3(k, l) = 2$ for every $k \ge 2$.

results.title: Solutions of a linear congruence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be integers, let $m$ be a positive integer, and let $d = \gcd(a, m)$. The congruence $a x \equiv b \pmod{m}$ has an integer solution if and only if $d \mid b$. If $d \mid b$, then exactly $d$ of the numbers $x \in \{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ are solutions. Moreover, if $x_0$ is a solution, then an integer $x$ is a solution if and only if $x \equiv x_0 + u \cdot (m / d) \pmod{m}$ for some integer $u$…

results.title: When a singleton set is sum-free
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$, $l$ and $m$ be natural numbers with $l \ge 1$, $m \ge 1$ and $m \nmid a$, and let $d = \gcd(a, m)$. If $d = 1$, then $\{a\}$ is not $l$-sum-free modulo $m$ if and only if $l \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$. If $d > 1$, then $\{a\}$ is not $l$-sum-free modulo $m$ if and only if $l \equiv 1 \pmod{m/d}$.

results.title: When the one-class modular Schur number equals one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $l$ and $m$ be natural numbers with $l \ge 2$, $m \ge 2$ and $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod m$. Then the generalized Schur number $S_m(1, l)$ modulo $m$ equals $1$ if and only if $l = 2$ or $2l \ge m + 1$.

results.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo 4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers and let $S_4(k, l)$ be the generalized Schur number modulo $4$. If $l \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, then $S_4(k, l) = 0$. Otherwise, if $k = 1$, or if $k \ge 2$ and $l \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, then $S_4(k, l) = 1$; and if $k \ge 2$ and $l \equiv 0$ or $2 \pmod 4$, then $S_4(k, l) = 3$.

results.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo 6
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers and let $S_6(k, l)$ be the generalized Schur number modulo $6$. If $l \equiv 1 \pmod 6$, then $S_6(k, l) = 0$. Otherwise $S_6(k, l) = 1$ if $k = 1$ and $l \ne 3$, or $k \ge 2$ and $l \equiv 4 \pmod 6$; $S_6(k, l) = 2$ if $k = 1$ and $l = 3$, or $k \ge 2$ and $l \equiv 3$ or $5 \pmod 6$; $S_6(k, l) = 3$ if $k = 2$, $l \equiv 0$ or $2 \pmod 6$, and $l \ge 6$; $S_6(k, l) = 4$ if…

results.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo 5
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers and let $S_5(k, l)$ be the generalized Schur number modulo $5$. If $l \equiv 1 \pmod 5$, then $S_5(k, l) = 0$. Otherwise $S_5(1, l) = 1$; if $k \in \{2, 3\}$ and $l \ne 2$, then $S_5(k, l) = k$; and if $k \in \{2, 3\}$ and $l = 2$, or if $k \ge 4$, then $S_5(k, l) = 4$.

results.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo 7
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers and let $S_7(k, l)$ be the generalized Schur number modulo $7$. If $l \equiv 1 \pmod 7$, then $S_7(k, l) = 0$. Otherwise $S_7(k, l) = 1$ if $k = 1$ and $l \ne 3$; $S_7(k, l) = 2$ if $k = 1$ and $l = 3$, or $k = 2$ and $l \ge 4$; $S_7(k, l) = 3$ if $k = 2$ and $l \in \{2, 3\}$, or $k = 3$ and $l \ge 5$; $S_7(k, l) = 4$ if $k = 4$ and $l \ge 5$; $S_7(k, l) = 5$ if $k = 3$ and…

results.title: Row lengths of the Connell triangle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $r$ and $j$, the length of row $j$ is $1 + r(j - 1)$, where $j - 1$ is read as $0$ when $j = 0$. For $j \ge 1$ this is the number of entries in row $j$ of the Connell $(m, r)$ triangle for every $m$; the source numbers rows from one, and the value at $j = 0$ is a convention.

results.title: First entries of the rows of the Connell triangle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $r$, the numbers $s_j$ are defined by $s_0 = s_1 = 1$ and $s_{j+1} = s_j + m(\ell_j - 1) + 1$ for $j \ge 1$, where $\ell_j = 1 + r(j - 1)$ is the length of row $j$. For $j \ge 1$, $s_j$ is the first entry of row $j$ of the Connell $(m, r)$ triangle: each row starts one above the last entry $s_j + m(\ell_j - 1)$ of the row before. The source numbers rows from one, and the value $s_0 = 1$…

results.title: Entries of the Connell triangle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$, $r$, $j$ and $k$, the entry with zero-based index $k$ in row $j$ of the Connell $(m, r)$ triangle is $s_j + mk$, where $s_j$ is the first entry of row $j$. The formula is used for every $k$, also at or beyond the row length.

results.title: Rows of the Connell triangle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$, $r$ and $j$, row $j$ of the Connell $(m, r)$ triangle is the finite set of the numbers $s_j + mk$ with $0 \le k < \ell_j$, where $s_j$ is the first entry of row $j$ and $\ell_j = 1 + r(j - 1)$ is its length, with $j - 1$ read as $0$ when $j = 0$.

results.title: Connell parameters
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A pair of natural numbers $(m, r)$ with $m \ge 2$ and $r \ge 1$; these are the admissible parameters of a Connell $(m, r)$ sequence.

results.title: Next position in the Connell triangle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $r$, the position following row $j$, zero-based column $k$, is row $j$, column $k + 1$ if $k + 1 < 1 + r(j - 1)$ (the length of row $j$, with $j - 1$ read as $0$ when $j = 0$), and row $j + 1$, column $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Position of a term in the Connell triangle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $r$, the position $p_n = (j_n, k_n)$ (row $j_n$, zero-based column $k_n$) of index $n \ge 0$ is defined by $p_0 = (1, 0)$ and $p_{n+1} = (j_n, k_n + 1)$ if $k_n + 1 < 1 + r(j_n - 1)$ (the length of row $j_n$, with $j_n - 1$ read as $0$ when $j_n = 0$), and $p_{n+1} = (j_n + 1, 0)$ otherwise.

results.title: Connell sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m \ge 2$ and $r \ge 1$, the Connell $(m, r)$ sequence $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ reads the Connell triangle row by row: row $j \ge 1$ has $\ell_j = 1 + r(j - 1)$ entries $s_j, s_j + m, \dots, s_j + m(\ell_j - 1)$, where $s_1 = 1$ and $s_{j+1} = s_j + m(\ell_j - 1) + 1$. Thus $a_n = s_j + mk$, where row $j$, zero-based column $k$ is the position reached from row $1$, column $0$ after $n$ steps, each step…

results.title: Cyclic labeling of the ladder perimeter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ and $s$ be natural numbers. Number the vertices of the ladder $P_n \times P_2$ along its perimeter by $0, 1, \dots, 2n - 1$, with $v_k$ at position $k - 1$ and $u_k$ at position $2n - k$ for $1 \le k \le n$. The cyclic label with offset $s$ of the position $i \in \{0, \dots, 2n - 1\}$ is $((i + s) \bmod 2n) + 1$.

results.title: Adjacency in the ladder graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Number the vertices of the ladder $P_n \times P_2$ along its perimeter by $0, 1, \dots, 2n-1$, with $v_k$ at position $k - 1$ and $u_k$ at position $2n - k$ for $1 \le k \le n$. Two positions $i, j \in \{0, \dots, 2n-1\}$ are adjacent when $j \equiv i + 1 \pmod{2n}$ or $i \equiv j + 1 \pmod{2n}$ (neighbours along the perimeter cycle), or when $i + j = 2n - 1$ (the rung joining $v_k$ and $u_k$).

results.title: Consecutive cyclic prime labeling of the ladder
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ and $s$ be natural numbers. Number the vertices of the ladder $P_n \times P_2$ along its perimeter by $0, 1, \dots, 2n - 1$, with $v_k$ at position $k - 1$ and $u_k$ at position $2n - k$ for $1 \le k \le n$. The offset $s$ gives a consecutive cyclic prime labeling of the ladder when $n > 0$ and, for all positions $i, j \in \{0, \dots, 2n - 1\}$ that are adjacent in the ladder graph, the cyclic labels of $i$…

results.title: Cyclic labels are positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $s$ and every position $i \in \{0, \dots, 2n-1\}$, the cyclic label of $i$ with offset $s$ is at least $1$.

results.title: Cyclic labels do not exceed the number of vertices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n > 0$ and $s$ and every position $i \in \{0, \dots, 2n-1\}$, the cyclic label of $i$ with offset $s$ is at most $2n$.

results.title: Range of the cyclic labels
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n > 0$ and $s$ and every position $i \in \{0, \dots, 2n-1\}$, the cyclic label $c$ of $i$ with offset $s$ satisfies $1 \le c \le 2n$.

results.title: The cyclic label of the first position with offset zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n > 0$ be a natural number and number the vertices of the ladder $P_n \times P_2$ along its perimeter by $0, 1, \dots, 2n - 1$, with $v_k$ at position $k - 1$ and $u_k$ at position $2n - k$ for $1 \le k \le n$. Then the cyclic label with offset $0$ of the position $0$ (the vertex $v_1$) is $1$.

results.title: Instances of EXACT COVER
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of EXACT COVER is a pair $(n, C)$ of a natural number $n$, the size of the universe $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, and a finite list $C$ of finite lists of natural numbers, the candidate subsets. That each entry of $C$ lists distinct elements of the universe is required by well-formedness, not by the type of instances.

results.title: Well-formed EXACT COVER instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, C)$ of EXACT COVER is well formed when every entry of $C$ is a list of pairwise distinct natural numbers, each less than $n$.

results.title: Feasible EXACT COVER instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, C)$ of EXACT COVER is feasible when $C$ has a sublist $S$, obtained by deleting some entries of $C$, such that for every natural number $x < n$ there is exactly one list that occurs in $S$ and contains $x$.

results.title: EXACT COVER as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem EXACT COVER accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of pairs of a natural number and a list of lists of natural numbers, to an instance of EXACT COVER that is well formed and feasible; bitstrings that do not decode are rejected.

results.title: EXACT COVER is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem EXACT COVER is in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
